title: Credible
coreMove: Move a claim from assertion into inspectable proof, witness, or human-scale evidence.
sourcePressure: The source centers belief through proof, witnesses, vivid detail, anti-authority, and human-scale statistics, anchored by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren, Pam Laffin, and translated numbers.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Thinking credibility means adding credentials, citations, or bigger numbers.

sourceAnchors.name: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says Barry Marshall and Robin Warren support the idea that vivid proof can make disbelief harder to hold
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren matter here because proof can push past what expert habit refuses to see.

sourceAnchors.name: Pam Laffin
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says Pam Laffin supports anti-authority credibility through lived cost rather than official status
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Pam Laffin carries credibility from cost, not credentials.

sourceAnchors.name: human-scale statistics
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says large statistics often fail until translated into human-scale terms people can feel without expertise
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A giant number starts to work only after it is translated into a scale the body understands.

hook: nobody believes the claim until a number appears
bring receipts as a generic line
counterintuition: credibility is not authority repeated without proof
examples: nonprofit dramatic photo from old package
restaurant portion test from old package

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a stall owner answering skeptical restaurant buyers
exampleSpecs.stakes: buyers drop the stall if freshness sounds like sales talk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel places the catch log, ice temperature reading, and stamped delivery tag beside the fish so buyers can judge the claim
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The cod still smells like clean salt, not fish

exampleSpecs.audience: an engineer defending track replacement to a finance committee
exampleSpecs.stakes: a delayed repair raises derailment risk on a commuter line
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars translates vibration readings into the number of loose bolts found on a single platform section and shows the inspection photos
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The committee room table trembles when the freight train passes outside

exampleSpecs.audience: a product manager deciding whether a claim can go on packaging
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bold claim could mislead families and trigger regulator scrutiny
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Can a parent test this?" Chiara asks, then rejects the claim until the lab result and use condition fit on the package
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Can a parent test this?" Chiara asks with the label proof in her hand

exampleSpecs.audience: a league director persuading coaches to follow removal rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: a player could return too soon if the evidence feels bureaucratic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: David brings a parent witness and the sideline checklist instead of a lecture from league headquarters
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 6:30 p.m., David clips the folded sideline checklist to a goalpost

exampleSpecs.audience: an auditor convincing a homeowner that attic sealing matters
exampleSpecs.stakes: the homeowner will spend money only if the leak is believable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Chidi ask the homeowner to predict the leak, then run a smoke pencil near the attic hatch until the draft appears
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You feel the hallway cool down when the attic hatch opens

exampleSpecs.audience: a librarian defending a teen program to trustees
exampleSpecs.stakes: the program loses evening staff if impact sounds soft
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anke pairs attendance numbers with one checkable tutoring schedule and a student work sample so trustees can inspect impact at human scale
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Anke one budget cycle to stop saying engagement

skillTargets: choose proof appropriate to a skeptical audience
translate large numbers into human scale
distinguish anti-authority credibility from mere anecdote
spot when vivid proof becomes theater rather than evidence

tryThisNowSpec: Find one claim in your message and add the nearest thing your audience can check: a witness, a test, a specific detail, or a human-scale translation.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
